title: Cevahir Zihin and Cevahir AI: a Living Evidence Mind, Living-Learning Research Reports and Technical Book
description:
Latest update (2026.11.15): Cevahir Zihin, a mind that learns by living. Not a Transformer. The model in this archive (zihin/) is a Living Evidence Mind, not a neural network: it has no weight matrices, embedding vectors, backpropagation or softmax attention. It keeps every relation as a tie and keeps each tie's graded evidence separately by where it came from (sensed, told, imitated, its own act, inferred, imagined); the trust in the four indirect origins (told, imitated, inferred, imagined) is learned from direct experience, and sensed evidence and its own acts are the reference. It reads what to expect from one rule, e = c(f - 1/2) + 1/2 with conviction c = W/(W+1) (the NARS truth-value expectation), and learns at every moment with no separate training phase. While its ledger is kept, the evidence of any single experience can be retracted exactly (exact for the evidence, not a replay of a life without it). Its attention is a Seven-Place Focus: seven units win the focus each moment (present items, the recognised lived context, its categories and frames, associations), so attention is local and readable; there is no context window, and the time per moment grows only slowly with lived memory.

Named findings, with their measurements, demonstrations and negative results (docs/ZIHIN_THEORY.md, research/living_mind_2026_11_15/NOTES.md): Members' Reading (a category speaks with what its members lived; on instances never told the asked dimension 100%/90% in two domains after 1500 experiences), Resemblance Vote (an exemplar-model vote; seeing 67-83%, new sounds of known synthetic voices 93-97%, chance 33%), Situation Resemblance, Felt Not-Knowing (not knowing is a measured inner state; "I do not know" is learned), Think-then-Speak, Trying in Hesitation (exploration: from imitating wrong code to passing code for six of six tiny tasks by round 4 with test results as consequences; 0% without them), Structural Imagination (a demonstration) and Shared-Stem Inference, Dream Sorting (dreams are kept with their claims and sorted true, false or open when life meets them), the Self Unit (a demonstration), Voice Credibility (learning to learn: a small gain in one direction only), and the One-Origin Row (239 to 69 bytes per tie with bit-identical results). The core runs on an ordinary CPU with no training phase; a moment takes about 4 ms on a mind with 3.25 million ties, and memory still grows linearly with lived data. The minds raised so far lived the author's private Turkish data and are not in this archive; a new mind starts empty, learns in every conversation, and runs with: python -m zihin (or .\cevahir.ps1 on Windows). No claim of consciousness, general intelligence or novelty is made: the one rule is the NARS expectation, the Resemblance Vote follows exemplar models, and the focus is a k-winners-take-all competition.

Versioned open-source research archive by Muhammed Yasin Yılmaz. Contains nine individually identified research reports/preprints (CEV-2026-01 through CEV-2026-09), reproducible computational experiments, preserved negative results, the Cevahir implementation, and a twelve-chapter Turkish technical book with an English reading guide.

The research asks how experience during operation can persistently, controllably and generalizably change a system's future computation and behavior. Studies examine experience-conditioned computation, representation search, persistence and transfer, credit assignment, learning-state transport, learned updates, recurrent-state acquisition, correction, and future-query state requirements. The general living-learning problem remains open.

The newest finite audit enumerates 61,575 histories and checks 712,632 content-informed label writes and 358,020 appends. Full records and limitations are included. These reports have not undergone external peer review. AI assistance was used for code, computational experiments, literature review and drafting. DOI registration identifies this archived version; it does not certify scientific correctness or establish novelty.

Start at docs/publications/README.md for the reports and docs/book/README.md for the book. This DOI covers the collection and code together, not separate DOI registrations for each report.

This second archive edition expands book chapters 3-6 with neural-network and embedding foundations, attention and Transformer mathematics, training methods, original-paper citations, dated industry comparisons, and solved exercises. Seven reproducible CPU example groups use actual Cevahir components; 99 selected neural-core, attention, MoE and training tests passed. This is an evolving educational manuscript, not a claim that every chapter is complete. The nine research reports retain their original findings and source records.

This third archive edition expands chapters 7-9 with checkpoint identity and resume, generation mathematics and cache, memory retrieval and tool orchestration: 15 new solved exercises and ten additional executed CPU example groups. It corrects calculator expression truncation found during code review, preserving the original negative observation. Seventy selected generation, agent, checkpoint and runtime tests passed. The book now contains 12 chapters, 115 second-level headings and 64 third-level headings; it remains an evolving manuscript.

This fourth archive edition adds the first broad living-learning campaign: 200 catalog propositions, 48 executable conditional comparisons, 3,456 paired outcomes, full discovery and confirmation records, source hashes, and negative controls. Thirty claims were supported, nine contradicted and nine inconclusive under a fixed synthetic rule; 152 catalog entries remain queued. The general problem remains open and the results have not undergone external peer review.

This fifth archive edition adds: CEV-11, a frozen confirmatory study of persistent knowledge writes into a fixed network (writing about 52 facts into one layer collapsed the model; the life test was not run and the report says why); a concept-address study (an external memory beat in-weight addressing by 58.2 points); optional forward-learning and absorbing-walk attention extensions with their studies; a cevahir_ai roof package with content keys, a registry with a hash-chained audit log and a PowerShell-like console; and a new core, Cevahir Zihin, that is not a Transformer: it learns while it runs, with no fixed dimension, vocabulary or training phase; knowledge is a growing structure of units and ties carrying source-resolved evidence with learned trust, and any single experience can be retracted exactly. Measured on two generated worlds (5 seeds): graded conviction, refinement without deletion, hidden classes recovered, no forgetting (a second domain leaves the first bit-identical), exact retraction, and generalisation to never-seen instances that improves with age (93%/81% after 600 experiences, 100%/90% after 1500) once a category is read from what its members lived; imitation followed by detachment by outcomes. A terminal chat answers watched dialogues, answers some unwatched questions by relations, stays silent when it knows nothing and stops a copied answer after negative feedback. Learning to learn came out negative; asking its own questions and imagination with a measured sense of reality are not built yet; against a small Transformer on the identical stream it generalises better to never-seen instances (90%/97% and 75%/95% against 67%/57%, 60%/50% online and 77%/67%, 53%/53% trained to convergence), keeps a first domain intact where the online Transformer forgets (1.00 vs 0.85 -> 0.74) and retracts exactly in milliseconds; this holds in the small-data regime only and the worlds are small. All negative results are kept. No claim of consciousness, general intelligence or novelty is made; the reports are not peer reviewed.
